commands.command: design: HumanGateCoordinator.validate() filters the presented GateSignature set down to only those that are unexcluded, resolved via the sealed IdentityRegistry, scope-matched, and within the policy's TTL as of the call's own 'at' timestamp; separation of duties is enforced by never letting one principal_id satisfy two distinct required_roles (a principal already credited toward one required role cannot also cover another). Because validate() is a pure function of (signatures, scope, at), calling it once at Human Gate resolution and again, completely unmodified, immediately before dispatch is what gives dual control its real meaning: a signature within TTL at resolution can have expired by dispatch time, and the identical check denies then exactly as it would for a fresh evaluation -- never trusting a stale resolution.

requirement_results.command: a quorum covering both required roles by two distinct, registered humans within TTL and correct scope resolves an approved Approval
fewer distinct valid signatories than the policy's minimum_signatories fails closed with QUORUM_NOT_MET
the identical real human signing for two distinct required roles is never counted as satisfying both -- separation of duties enforced structurally, not merely checked
a third distinct signatory duplicating an already-covered role does not substitute for coverage of a still-uncovered required role
a signature outside the policy's TTL as of the evaluation time is excluded and denies the gate even though it was valid when first granted
a signature scoped to a different resource than the action being decided is excluded and denies the gate
the action's own proposer can never satisfy any required role, even with an otherwise fully valid signature
a signature from a principal_id never registered in the sealed IdentityRegistry is never counted

the identical, unmodified validation re-run at a later dispatch-time timestamp denies an approval that was genuinely valid at resolution time, once TTL has elapsed in between -- proving real revalidation, not a cached or trusted-forever decision
an injected control-plane check that raises blocks the Approval even though quorum and role coverage would otherwise succeed, propagating the real error unwrapped
a real bounded HTTP probe against a genuinely closed local port, driven through OCOR-DEV-0021's sealed fail-closed helpers, blocks the Approval rather than silently defaulting to permit
a GateSignature's content-addressed integrity_digest is deterministic for identical semantic fields and changes when any one of them changes

HumanGateCoordinator's own resolved Approval is the identical sealed OCOR-DEV-0030 type GovernedActionEngine.execute already accepts, driving a real end-to-end governed action to a simulated effect with no adapter needed
full local pytest regression with a real live PostgreSQL DSN set, no new failures versus the pre-existing sandbox baseline (the two known interpreter-pin failures are unrelated and pre-existing)

residual_risks: This task's dual-control revalidation relies entirely on the caller invoking HumanGateCoordinator.validate() a second time immediately before dispatch with the then-current timestamp; it does not itself intercept or schedule the dispatch call -- a future integration task wiring this into a real dispatch pipeline must actually make that second call, not merely construct the coordinator once.

GateSignature's integrity_digest is a content-addressed, tamper-evident binding via the shared RFC 8785 kernel canonicalizer, not a real asymmetric cryptographic signature -- no PKI/signing infrastructure exists in this delivery's scope, the same honesty already established by OCOR-DEV-0028's unsigned signature_envelope_ref placeholder.

The optional control_check hook lets a caller wire a real live control-plane probe (as this task's own fault-injection test does against a genuinely unreachable port via OCOR-DEV-0021's sealed helpers), but human_gate.py itself performs no live network call by default -- a production caller must supply one for the fail-closed control-plane property to actually apply at runtime.

The pre-existing local-venv gap noted in prior evidence (uv cannot resolve the exact 3.12.11 interpreter in this sandbox) is unchanged and out of this task's scope; it produces the same 2 pre-existing, unrelated regression failures documented in every prior evidence file this session.
